document.title: Message to Taliban (State 175415)
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), New Documents Detail America's Strategic Response to 9/11
document.note: [Secret/Nodis/Eyes Only] The U.S. asks ISI chief Mahmoud or Musharraf to deliver a message to the Taliban: hand over al-Qaida leaders or face a devastating response, Taliban leaders will be held personally responsible, and 'every pillar of the Taliban regime will be destroyed.'

mentions.quote: SEEK IMMEDIATE APPOINTMENT WITH GENERAL MAHMUD TO REQUEST THAT EITHER HE OR PRESIDENT MUSHARRAF IMMEDIATELY DELIVER

events.description: State Department sends NODIS cable instructing Ambassador Chamberlin to have General Mahmud or Musharraf deliver a warning to Mullah Omar demanding handover of al-Qa'ida leaders and closure of terrorist camps.

State Department sends NIACT cable instructing Ambassador Chamberlin to have Mahmud or Musharraf deliver a warning to Mullah Omar: hand over al-Qaida leaders, close camps, or the Taliban regime will be destroyed.
The cable was drafted (SA:CBROCCA) and approved by the Deputy Secretary.

relationships.detail: Instructed to seek immediate appointment to request he or Musharraf deliver the message.
relationships.quote: SHOULD SEEK IMMEDIATE APPOINTMENT WITH GENERAL MAHMUD

relationships.detail: Asked to deliver US warning message to Mullah Omar (intermediary).
relationships.quote: IMMEDIATELY DELIVER THE FOLLOWING MESSAGE TO MULLAH OMAR

relationships.detail: Alternative messenger for the US warning.
relationships.quote: EITHER HE OR PRESIDENT MUSHARRAF IMMEDIATELY DELIVER

relationships.detail: Addressed as Taliban leader responsible for regime's actions.
relationships.quote: WE WILL HOLD LEADERS OF THE TALIBAN PERSONALLY RESPONSIBLE

relationships.detail: US demands the Taliban hand over al-Qa'ida leaders and close terrorist camps, implying the Taliban host them.
relationships.quote: HAND OVER ALL AL-QAIDA LEADERS, TO CLOSE THE TERRORISTS' CAMPS

relationships.detail: Cable approved by Deputy Secretary and sent to the ambassador.
The Department of State (SECSTATE) sent a NIACT IMMEDIATE cable to the embassy in Islamabad.
relationships.quote: FM SECSTATE WASHDC TO AMEMBASSY ISLAMABAD NIACT IMMEDIATE

relationships.detail: Chamberlin is instructed to seek an immediate appointment with Mahmud to request delivery of a message.
relationships.quote: AMBASSADOR CHAMBERLIN SHOULD SEEK IMMEDIATE APPOINTMENT WITH GENERAL MAHMUD

relationships.detail: Chamberlin asks that Mahmud or Musharraf deliver the message to Mullah Omar.
relationships.quote: REQUEST THAT EITHER HE OR PRESIDENT MUSHARRAF IMMEDIATELY DELIVER THE FOLLOWING MESSAGE TO MULLAH OMAR

relationships.detail: The US message warns the Taliban of devastating response and destruction of the regime if attacks occur.
relationships.quote: EVERY PILLAR OF THE TALIBAN REGIME WILL BE DESTROYED.

relationships.detail: The US demands the Taliban hand over all al-Qaida leaders and close its camps.
relationships.quote: HAND OVER ALL AL-QAIDA LEADERS, TO CLOSE THE TERRORISTS' CAMPS

relationships.detail: Attackers connected to Afghanistan, and al-Qaida camps there, are the subject of the warning.
relationships.quote: IF ANY PERSON OR GROUP CONNECTED IN ANY WAY TO AFGHANISTAN CONDUCTS A TERRORIST ATTACK

relationships.detail: Armitage is Deputy Secretary of State and classified/approved the cable.
relationships.quote: CLASSIFIED BY RICHARD L. ARMITAGE, DEPUTY SECRETARY OF STATE

relationships.detail: The cable is signed POWELL, as Secretary of State.
Chamberlin is the ambassador to whom the cable is addressed.
Islamabad is in Pakistan, where Mahmud and Musharraf are located.

key_claims: The US told the Taliban it had information that al-Qa'ida was planning additional terrorist attacks.
The US demanded the Taliban hand over all al-Qa'ida leaders and close terrorist camps.
The US threatened that every pillar of the Taliban regime would be destroyed.
The US used Pakistani leaders (General Mahmud or Musharraf) as intermediaries to Mullah Omar.
The US said it would hold Taliban leaders personally responsible for terrorist attacks connected to Afghanistan.
